exposure: travel time between household and hospital
cohort: The cohort consisted of asphyxiated newborns admitted to Tosamaganga Hospital in Tanzania between January 2019 and June 2022, defined by an Apgar score < 7 at 5 minutes and birth weight > 1500g, excluding those with visible congenital malformations.
finding: Mortality among asphyxiated newborns in rural Tanzania was high (19.1%), and factors such as outborn status, lower Apgar scores, convulsions, longer travel time to hospital, and female sex were associated with increased risk of mortality or neurodevelopmental impairment.
